findings.location: src/keycloak/admin-port.ts createHumanUser 400 branch (isPersonNameCharacterError checked before isPersonNameLengthError, both via .some() over the full fieldErrors array)
findings.issue: If a single KC 400 body somehow carried BOTH a character-class error (e.g. firstName='Bot #1') AND a length-class error (e.g. lastName 300 chars) in the same {errors:[...]} array — a contrived but not provably impossible combination — isPersonNameCharacterError's .some() matches first and the request throws NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS, never reaching the isPersonNameLengthError check at all. The owner would fix the character problem, resubmit, and only then discover the separately-genuine length problem as a second round trip. Not a regression introduced by this task and not incorrect (the NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS message IS honest and true) — it is the exact same single-error-per-response limitation T-0748's own ux-review already flagged and accepted as non-blocking (T-0748.ux-review.json F-2), now extended by one more sibling class. judge could not construct a live KC body exhibiting both classes simultaneously on the same two fields to confirm this is reachable in practice (KC's declarative profile appears to run person-name-prohibited-characters and length as independent validators per field, but a single request only has 2 fields — firstName/lastName — so at most 2 distinct field-level errors, and this task's own live probes never produced a mixed character+length pair).
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. Same disposition as T-0748's own F-2 precedent — aggregating multiple field errors into one response would be a form-wide redesign out of scope here.

findings.location: docs/tasks/T-0762.pr-handoff.json AC-3 / src/__tests__/admin-port.test.ts AP-10 case 4 (mixed {errors:[email-bad, firstName-too-long]} shape)
findings.issue: Unlike AC-1/AC-2 (single-field and both-fields-over-cap), which the builder's spec.md §3 documents as directly live-probed against t-0633-keycloak-1 and which judge independently re-probed byte-identical (see acceptance_coverage below), the AC-3 mixed email+length {errors:[...]} shape is a synthesized test body, not an independently live-confirmed one — judge did not find a way to make KC itself reject both a malformed email AND an over-length name in the same POST (KC's email-format check appears to run in a different validation pass than the declarative user-profile length check, and judge's own attempts to combine them still only surfaced one error at a time in practice). The array *structure* itself (multiple {field,errorMessage} entries) IS live-confirmed (probe 2, both-fields-over-cap), so the parser codepath is real; only the specific mixed-content payload is unverified against a live realm.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking — same evidentiary class as T-0748's own AC-2 (mixed shape asserted via constructed stub body, not independently reproduced live either). Flagged for the record only.
